scenes.en: Here's why, and when to worry.
scenes.say: Is your eyelid jumping on its own? Here's why it happens, and when to worry.

scenes.en: A tiny eyelid muscle keeps firing. Usually harmless.
scenes.say: A tiny muscle in your eyelid keeps firing on its own. It feels strange, but it's usually harmless, and it stops by itself.

scenes.en: Poor sleep, stress, too much tea or coffee, long screen time
scenes.say: The common triggers are poor sleep, stress, too much tea or coffee, and long hours on screens.

scenes.en: Dry, tired eyes can also set off twitching.
scenes.say: Did you know? Dry, tired eyes can also set off twitching. So can eye strain from glasses with the wrong power.

scenes.en: Sleep 7–8 hours. Cut caffeine. Take screen breaks. Warm compress.
scenes.say: Sleep seven to eight hours. Cut down on caffeine. Take regular screen breaks, and try a warm compress on closed eyes.

scenes.en: It lasts weeks, the eyelid shuts fully, or other face muscles twitch
scenes.say: See a doctor if it lasts more than a few weeks, if your eyelid closes completely, or if other parts of your face start twitching.

scenes.en: A simple eye test checks if you need glasses.
scenes.say: Uncorrected power can strain your eyes too. Get a simple eye test, and rule it out.
